tldr: The paper introduces IMP-MARL, an open-source suite of MARL environments for large-scale Infrastructure Management Planning with up to 100 agents, benchmarking cooperative MARL methods against expert-based heuristic policies.
contributions: Introduction of IMP-MARL, a novel open-source suite of environments for scalable MARL-based infrastructure management planning.
Extensive benchmark campaign testing seven cooperative MARL methods (five CTDE, one centralized, one decentralized) against expert-based heuristic policies in IMP environments with up to 100 agents.
Public release of source code for reproducibility and future comparisons.
methods: The paper formulates Infrastructure Management Planning as a Dec-POMDP where each agent manages one component, deciding between do-nothing, inspect, or repair actions to minimize costs while cooperating to minimize system failure risk. Three environment sets are provided: k-out-of-n systems, correlated k-out-of-n systems, and offshore wind farm environments. Seven RL methods are benchmarked: DQN (fully centralized), IQL (fully decentralized), and five CTDE methods (QMIX, QVMix, QPLEX, COMA, FACMAC), all compared against expert-based heuristic policies from the reliability engineering community.
results: Centralized training with decentralized execution (CTDE) methods scale better with the number of agents than fully centralized or decentralized RL approaches. CTDE methods outperform expert-based heuristic policies in most IMP environments. However, the relative performance benefit of cooperative MARL decreases in environments with over 50 agents. In certain environments, MARL policies exhibit high variance and sometimes underperform expert-based heuristic policies.
limitations: The relative performance benefit of cooperative MARL methods decreases in environments with over 50 agents.
In certain environments, cooperative MARL policies are characterized by high variance and can underperform expert-based heuristic policies.
Remaining cooperation and scalability challenges were identified that future MARL methods need to address.
